deities: Shiva (Shiva Lingam in the sanctum; 58-ft concrete Gangadhareshwara sculpture in the complex)
festivals: Utsavam (annual festival in the Malayalam month of Makaram, January-February)

history.dynasty: Believed to date to the Pandya dynasty period (8th century claim - traditional attribution, not archaeologically verified); the 58-ft sculpture was commissioned by the Aazhimala Shiva Temple Devaswom Trust and sculpted 2014-2020 by P. S. Devadathan
history.period: Traditional claim of 8th-century origin; architecture described as Dravidian style similar to Tamil Nadu temples; the Gangadhareshwara sculpture was constructed 2 April 2014 to 31 December 2020
history.summary: The Azhimala (Aazhimala) Shiva Temple is a cliffside Hindu temple at Pulinkudi, 0.8 km off the Vizhinjam-Poovar road, overlooking the Arabian Sea - its name joins the Malayalam 'aazhi' (sea) and 'mala' (hill). Local legend links it to the Mahabharata: the Pandavas are said to have sheltered in the nearby caves during exile, and Bhima is said to have struck a rock (with knee or elbow - accounts differ) to create a freshwater stream for Draupadi; the stream still flows from a cave. Originally called Pulinkudi Sree Mahadeva Temple, it is famed for India's tallest Gangadhareshwara sculpture - an 18 m (58 ft) concrete seated Shiva holding trident, damaru and Ganga in his matted locks, sculpted by 29-year-old native artist P. S. Devadathan over nearly six years and unveiled 31 December 2020. A 3,500 sq ft meditation hall (Dhyana Mandapam) sits beneath the statue. Governed by the Aazhimala Shiva Temple Devaswom Trust; note - one source mentions Sree Narayana Guru's wish to build a Shiva temple here, but details are thin (verify).

name: Azhimala Shiva Temple
town: Azhimala, near Vizhinjam (CSV town 'Thiruvananthapuram' is approximate; the temple is ~16-17 km south of the city at Pulinkudi, Kottukal panchayat)
town_description: Vizhinjam is an ancient seaport town on the Arabian Sea coast about 16 km south of Thiruvananthapuram city. Known since early historic times as a maritime trade centre of the Ay and Venad kingdoms, it is now dominated by the Vizhinjam International Deepwater Transshipment Port, alongside a traditional fishing harbour and the Kovalam beach belt to its north. Azhimala (Pulinkudi) is a rocky headland on the Vizhinjam-Poovar road, prized for its cliff-and-sea views.

travel.road: 0.8 km off the Vizhinjam-Poovar road; steep narrow approach road - cars and autos can reach the temple door, buses park ~1 km away (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the statue viewpoint is best in the morning and late afternoon light
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not reliably published (verify); one video source mentions a nominal entry fee (₹100) for the cave/meditation hall with photography prohibited (verify)
